originalTitle: Tusk'a göre, Ukrayna'nın müttefikleri askeri tatbikat yaparken Rus füzesi Polonya'ya isabet etti
titleEn: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
headline: BBC'nin aktardığına göre, Ukrayna müttefikleri tatbikat yaparken Rus füzesi Polonya'ya isabet etti.
details: Füze, Ukrayna sınırına yaklaşık 50 km mesafedeki Nowy Lipowiec kırsalına düştü.
Olayda can kaybı veya hasar bildirilmezken, Varşova bunu "provokasyon" olarak nitelendirdi.
NATO Genel Sekreteri Rutte, "Polonya hava sahasının ciddi ihlallerini" kınadı.
brief: Polonya Başbakanı Tusk, Batı askeri tatbikatları sırasında meydana gelen olayın tesadüf olmadığını belirtti. NATO, ihlallere yanıt olarak jetlerin havalandığını duyurdu.
summary: BBC'nin haberine göre, Ukrayna'nın müttefiklerinin askeri tatbikat yaptığı sırada Rusya'ya ait bir seyir füzesi Polonya hava sahasını ihlal ederek ülkenin güneydoğusundaki Nowy Lipowiec kırsalına düştü. Polonya Başbakanı Donald Tusk, olayın Batı askeri tatbikatları devam ederken meydana gelmesinin tesadüf olmadığını ifade etti. Olayda herhangi bir can kaybı veya hasar bildirilmezken, Varşova bu durumu Moskova'dan gelen bir "provokasyon" olarak değerlendirdi. NATO Genel Sekreteri Mark Rutte, "Polonya hava sahasının ciddi ihlallerini" kınayarak NATO jetlerinin yanıt olarak havalandığını belirtti. Bu olay, Rusya'nın 2022'deki tam kapsamlı işgalden bu yana Ukrayna'ya yönelik en büyük hava saldırılarından biri sırasında gerçekleşti.

sourceText: BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat World Africa Asia Australia Europe Latin America Middle East Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk Figure caption, Watch: CCTV shows explosion after Poland says airspace violated by Russian missile Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region. Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow. Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border. The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact". The moment of impact was caught by a camera on a farm, and officials later made clear there was no risk to residents. Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near Mołodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz. He called the incursion into Polish airspace a "provocation" from Russia and said he would be asking Nato for additional support. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said Nato jets had been scrambled in response. "This incident is clearly dangerous - a consequence of Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine," said Rutte, who was due to visit Warsaw on Saturday. A UK- and France-led exercise called Koalicja 2026 is currently taking place in southeastern Poland involving 11 countries that are part of the West's Coalition of the Willing group in preparation for a potential peace deal in Ukraine. "It is no coincidence that these objects landed near the site where military manoeuvres by a 'coalition of the willing' supported by Polish troops are taking place in Nowa Dęba," Tusk told reporters on Friday. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, who was visiting Poland on Friday, said: "The impact of Russia's illegal war is being felt across Ukraine and increasingly in neighbouring countries."
